hard_link.why_hard: A checked reduction [L-gct-077] turns a larger bound for the permanent into one statement: a linear bound on the dimension of linear spaces of matrices on which the permanent of the all-ones matrix plus a variable matrix stays constant. No proof route has survived yet, and today a complex space was found that real-number searches had missed, so the small-case evidence is being redone.

target.beyond: The target is claimed in unrefereed 2026 reports, not verified by this project. No comparison of our checked statements with the literature is made here until a specialist has answered.
target.plain: Checked: over the complex numbers, an m by m permanent written as a determinant of affine forms, or as a limit of such determinants, needs size n with 3n at least 2m^2 - 10m + 11 [L-gct-070]. How this statement stands against published work is with a specialist and is not claimed here. The program's target is a cubic bound that unrefereed 2026 reports claim; this project has not verified it and has no proof route to it at present.

hard_link.title: Grid criterion: if hard row-even tables and easy tables are both rare at size s, a 1-local fixed-format map sends even inputs into MCSP and odd inputs out
hard_link.why_hard: Whether such a reduction exists turns on a fine comparison of average circuit sizes of two kinds of truth tables, finer than any known method resolves; it cannot be tested on small cases either. The question is parked and has been put to a specialist.

target.beyond: Adapts Murray and Williams, Theory of Computing 2017, from MCSP to partial MCSP; it formalizes an obstacle and does not remove one.
target.plain: Checked: if finding small circuits for partially specified functions is NP-hard under ordinary reductions, then exponential time contains a problem outside NP intersect P/poly [L-meta-016]; and parity of n inputs needs exactly 4(n - 1) gates in our basis [L-meta-026, L-meta-031], a known result. For reductions of parity that read few input bits per output bit, a construction and an obstruction are both checked, far apart; the target is to close the gap between them. Nothing of that is checked.
target.title: No reduction of parity to MCSP in which each output bit reads one input bit, at polynomial length

hard_link.why_hard: The program's first recorded hard link was refuted by the checker [L-alg-004]: as defined, one inference step could assert the pigeonhole principle itself. This restatement uses a rule that can be checked step by step; an adversary's attempt to refute it the same way failed. It has no proof route and the program is parked.

strategy_update.text: The exchange for one stacked AND gate is now argued on paper on both of its halves (a conjecture until checked, with readers from other seats trying to break it): a smallest circuit for a plane-like graph with exactly one AND gate stacked above another has a no-larger circuit with none. Where it is stuck, exactly: two stacked gates that interact, where a size formula on paper leaves three small named shapes uncovered. Under attack now: those three shapes.
